lead.hed: Kadena logistics Airmen issued simulated weapons during Beverly Sword
lead.insight: An Air Force release from Kadena Air Base says the 18th Logistics Readiness Squadron issued simulated weapons, protective gear, and bedrolls to Airmen on Oct. 27 as part of Exercise Beverly Sword 27-1. Master Sgt. Justen Rodriguez, a fuels contract officer, said the drill is meant to familiarize Airmen with weapons handling before a deployment. Senior Airman Major Mclemore of the 18th Comptroller Squadron said selective arming is how the wing makes sure Airmen outside traditional combat jobs are ready. The release says the exercise tests the 18th Wing's ability to project airpower and deter aggression.
lead.image_credit: Senior Airman Amy Kelley · DVIDS 10050396 · Public domain · Airmen wait for gear during Exercise Beverly Sword 27-1, Kadena Air Base, Japan, Oct. 27, 2026.

political.hed: The United States picked Poland to host a European PAC-3 maintenance hub
political.insight: Defense News reported from Warsaw that the United States selected Poland to host a new European maintenance facility for Patriot Advanced Capability-3 interceptors. Pentagon acquisition chief Michael Duffey said the hub puts sustainment on NATO's eastern front. The statement said Germany, the Netherlands, and Sweden will lead supply-chain work. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Tuesday that Poland had competed against several other countries for the site. The article does not give an opening date.

political.hed: India's defense secretary says Europe's rearmament is lifting Indian ammunition exports
political.insight: Defense News reported Tuesday that Indian Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh, speaking Oct. 23 in New Delhi, tied rising exports to the European Union's ReArm Europe plan and India's larger manufacturing base. He cited a Bloomberg tally, drawn from Trade Data Monitor, that India exported at least $872 million in ammunition in the four years after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, more than 1,600 percent above the prior four years. Named buyers include Romania, Slovenia, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Croatia, and Poland. The article says the goods include artillery shells, small-caliber rounds, mortars, and propellants.

political.hed: Law & Liberty asks whether France's center can hold after the October looting
political.insight: Theodore Dalrymple's Tuesday essay opens on the Oct. 17 riots he calls a jacquerie. He writes that young men of Muslim background were disproportionately involved, and that French law bars ethnic statistics, so precise figures will not exist. He rejects a straight line from Islam to the looting. He says a considerable share of young French people already think political violence is justified, with 2027 elections ahead. It is an argument, not a vote count.

tech.hed: About 2,000 Marines ended the Darwin rotation as the first certified special-purpose task force
tech.insight: A Marine Corps release from Camp Pendleton says about 2,000 Marines and Sailors of Marine Rotational Force-Darwin 26 finished a deployment across Australia and the Indo-Pacific. It was the program's 15th rotation, and the first time the force was certified as a Special Purpose Marine Air-Ground Task Force. Col. George Flynn, commanding officer of MRF-D 26.3, said the rotation trained with the Australian Defence Force in Render Safe, Predators Run, Southern Jackaroo, and Capital Reach. From March through October the force also trained in the Philippines, New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, French Polynesia, and Indonesia. Certification was completed during Balikatan, April 20 through May 8.

tech.hed: An Army Pacific commander wants high-altitude balloons that can watch, relay, and strike
tech.insight: Defense News reported Tuesday that Maj. Gen. Bernard Harrington, commander of the 7th Infantry Division and Multi-Domain Command-Pacific, said at the Association of the U.S. Army conference that high-altitude balloons could give the Pacific a cheaper, lower-signature way to watch a battlefield, pass communications, and strike. His command combines the 7th Infantry Division's ground units with the 1st Multi-Domain Task Force's long-range fires. He said the aim is to open windows in China's anti-access network. The article does not name a funded program or a fielding date.

tech.hed: Keen Sword's first week put 56,000 troops on anti-ship drills, a jet boat, and a camera drone
tech.insight: A U.S. Forces Japan release from Tokyo says Keen Sword 27 is about halfway through, with more than 56,000 allied and partner forces already training on the ground, at sea, in the air, in space, and in cyberspace. Japan and the United States ran a large anti-ship drill that tied sea, air, land, space, and cyber units to one inbound threat. At Iwakuni, a Typhoon unmanned surface vessel — about 11 feet, jet-powered, able to hold above 50 knots — ran a naval interception demonstration. Crews also flew a Honey Badger X8 camera drone. At four bases, engineers practiced filling runway craters so aircraft can keep flying.

culture.hed: First Things sets the Book of Job beside a woman who can no longer speak
culture.insight: A Tuesday First Things essay opens by saying Job lost everything, then describes a woman who has lost speech, walking, and the names of her children while the house and the money still exist. She sits in a wheelchair. Job could still protest. She groans or yells, and words that sound like speech carry no meaning. It is a meditation on suffering, not a policy item.
